# Introduction

The main goals of this lab are for you to 1) get more familiar with the CS01 data and 2) for you to have one clean dataset by the end of lab - combining the blood, oral fluid, and breath datasets.

# Getting started

To get started, find your `lab02-<your GitHub username>` repo in the [course GitHub organization](https://github.com/COGS137-FA26), clone the repo (using SSH) into RStudio on datahub. And, then you're ready to go!

# Packages

This lab uses two packages: `tidyverse` (which includes `dplyr`, the package you'll be using most in this lab) and `janitor` (for `clean_names()`). Both are loaded for you in the `load-packages` chunk of the provided .qmd template.

# Data

The three data files you'll be using in this lab have been provided in the `data/` folder. You'll see the following three lines in the provided .qmd template for this lab, which, when run, will read each of the files into R for you:

``` r
WB <- read_csv("data/Blood.csv")
OF <- read_csv("data/OF.csv")
BR <- read_csv("data/Breath.csv")
```

# Exercises

### Exercise 1: **Whole Blood**

Explore

### Exercise 2: **Oral Fluid**

In a *similar* manner to how the whole blood data were wrangled and cleaned, carry out wrangling on the oral fluid dataset, accomplishing the following:

-   `Treatment` re-coded and re-leveled as was done with WB
-   `Group` re-coded to match the levels in WB: `"Experienced user"` → `"Frequent user"` and `"Not experienced user"` → `"Occasional user"`
-   column names cleaned using `clean_names()` as with WB
-   The following columns renamed: `thcoh = x11_oh_thc`; `thcv = thc_v`; `fluid_type=fluid`
-   A `timepoint` column (using `case_when()` as in lecture) with the following time windows (note these are different than WB): `"pre-smoking","0-30 min","31-90 min","91-180 min", "181-210 min", "211-240 min","241-270 min", "271+ min"`

### Exercise 3: **Breath**

In a *similar* manner to both previous datasets, carry out wrangling on the breath dataset, accomplishing the following:

-   `Treatment` re-coded and re-leveled as was done with WB/OF
-   `Group` re-coded to match the levels in WB: `"Experienced user"` → `"Frequent user"` and `"Not experienced user"` → `"Occasional user"`
-   column names cleaned using `clean_names()` as with WB/OF
-   The following columns renamed: `thc = thc_pg_pad`; `fluid_type=fluid`
-   A `timepoint` column (using `case_when()` as in lecture) with the following time windows (note these are different than WB/OF): `"pre-smoking","0-40 min","41-90 min", "91-180 min", "181-210 min", "211-240 min", "241-270 min", "271+ min"`

### Exercise 4: **Combine** (*time-permitting*)

Combine all three datasets into a single dataframe. Note that there is a function in `dplyr` called `bind_rows()` for accomplishing such a task.

You'll likely have to look up the documentation for `bind_rows()`, as it has not been directly covered in class yet.

::: callout-note
Going forward (in lecture and in CS01), all of this cleaning lives in a single function, `clean_cs01()` (in `src/cs01_functions.R`), which does the same thing for each dataset. Doing it by hand here is how you'll understand what that function is doing.
:::

### Exercise 5: **Summarize**

In your own words (no code needed), describe the wrangling that was done overall, focusing on why it was done or what it achieved, rather than on specific lines of code.
